Hing or Hängte? German B1 Hängen Meaning Practice

Compare the position verb hängen with the act of hanging something up. Practise hing/gehangen and hängte/gehängt in past-tense contexts.

B1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions + writing task

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Try the exercisesWrite your own sentence

Understand the difference

In the standard distinction, hängen describing a position uses strong past forms: Das Schild hing dort; es hat dort gehangen. Hängen meaning to put something into a hanging position takes an object and weak past forms: Sie hängte das Schild auf; sie hat es aufgehängt.

Common mistake to avoid

The present-tense forms look alike. Use the role of the subject and whether an object is being placed to decide the past-tense pattern.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Compare the meaning and sentence pattern, rather than choosing by English translation alone.

Worked example 1Das Schild hing gestern noch am Zaun.The sign was still hanging on the fence yesterday.
Worked example 2Sie hängte das Schild an einen Pfosten.She hung the sign on a post.
Worked example 3Die Mäntel haben im Flur gehangen.The coats hung in the hallway.
Worked example 4Wir haben die Mäntel an die Haken gehängt.We hung the coats on the hooks.

Practice: choose the right word

Use Präteritum or Partizip II as requested, distinguishing an existing position from the act of hanging something. Try each question before opening the answer. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Das Foto ___ früher über dem Schreibtisch. (position, Präteritum)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: hing

The position verb uses the strong past form hing.

Question 2. Er ___ das Foto an die Wand. (placement, Präteritum)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: hängte

With a placement object, use the weak form hängte.

Question 3. Der Spiegel hat jahrelang dort ___. (position, Partizip II)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: gehangen

The standard position participle is gehangen.

Question 4. Ich habe die Tasche an den Haken ___. (placement, Partizip II)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: gehängt

The standard placement participle is gehängt.

Use it in your own sentence

Describe hanging up a coat and where it hung yesterday.

Try writing your answer before reading the model below. Other natural answers are possible.

One possible answer

Ich habe den Mantel aufgehängt. Gestern hing er noch im Flur.

Check your wording: Placement uses aufgehängt; the position uses strong past hing.

What to practise next

Write a new context for each word. Explain which meaning or object pattern makes your choice natural; some contexts allow both.

Try the gaps again on another day without reading the explanation first. If a choice is still unclear, use the linked grammar foundation before moving to another topic.
